title: SkillAlign: Aligning Skill Interfaces for LLM-based Agents
abstract: arXiv:2609.07255v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language-model agents increasingly rely on skills: reusable procedural knowledge for reasoning, tool use, and interaction. Existing work studies how skills are acquired, retrieved, compressed, or composed, but often assumes that once a skill is selected, its interface to the agent is fixed. We argue that this overlooks a key source of skill utility: the same skill can help, distract, or mislead depending on how it is exposed. We propose SkillAlign, a provider-agnostic framework that represents candidate skills as multi-view procedural cards and renders them through alternative exposure interfaces, including full instructions, hints, compressed summaries, workflows, or no exposure. This enables counterfactual evaluation where the task, agent, and candidate skills are fixed while only the exposure interface varies. translated_title: SkillAlign：面向基于大语言模型智能体的技能接口对齐
translated_abstract: 语言模型智能体越来越依赖技能：即用于推理、工具使用和交互的可复用程序性知识。现有工作研究技能如何被获取、检索、压缩或组合，但通常假设一旦技能被选中，其面向智能体的接口就是固定的。我们认为这忽视了一个关键的技能效用来源：同一技能可能因其暴露方式的不同而起到帮助、分散注意力或误导的作用。我们提出 SkillAlign，一个与提供者无关的框架，它将候选技能表示为多视图程序卡片，并通过多种可替代的暴露接口进行呈现，包括完整指令、提示、压缩摘要、工作流或不暴露。这使得反事实评估成为可能：任务、智能体和候选技能保持不变，而仅改变暴露接口。在 ALFWorld 和 SkillsBench 上的实验表明，暴露形式会显著影响任务成功率和呈现的上下文成本，并且……
tldr: SkillAlign 提出一个与提供者无关的框架，将技能表示为多视图程序卡片并通过多种暴露接口呈现，利用反事实评估证明同一技能的暴露方式会显著影响大语言模型智能体的任务成功率和上下文成本。
en_tdlr: SkillAlign proposes a provider-agnostic framework that represents skills as multi-view procedural cards rendered through alternative exposure interfaces, using counterfactual evaluation to show that how a skill is exposed substantially affects LLM agent task success and context cost.
